concepts.title: Me
concepts.summary: The reader: about 80 kg, commutes with a laptop bag, budget up to 3,500, lives on a second floor with no lift, parks at an outdoor rack at work.

prov.quote: I'm about 80 kg, and I'd carry a laptop bag. Budget up to 3500

concepts.title: My commute
concepts.summary: 14 km each way, 28 km a day, roughly 6,000 km a year, with one real hill; the reader doesn't want to arrive sweaty.

prov.quote: 14 km each way, one real hill
your 6,000 km a year

concepts.title: The hill
concepts.summary: The one climb on the commute: about 800 m long, peaking near an 8 percent grade.

prov.quote: About 800 metres long, maybe 8 percent at the steepest

concepts.title: Hill climbing
concepts.summary: Climb the 800 m, 8 percent hill easily enough to arrive at work without sweating; judged mainly by motor type and torque.

prov.quote: I really don't want to arrive sweaty

concepts.title: Low maintenance
concepts.summary: Little cleaning, oiling and part replacement for a daily all-weather commuter.

prov.quote: low maintenance

concepts.title: Weight for the stairs
concepts.summary: Light enough to carry up two flights daily; 23–24 kg is noticeably easier than 26 kg, and removing the battery saves about 2.5–3 kg.

prov.quote: My flat is on the second floor with no lift.

concepts.title: Theft protection
concepts.summary: How well the bike can be secured at an outdoor work rack, beyond just a lock.

prov.quote: Theft worries me.

concepts.title: Price
concepts.summary: Purchase price within a 3,500 budget; a secondary concern after the four main priorities.

prov.quote: Price second.

concepts.title: Torque
concepts.summary: The key number for hill climbing: 60–85 Nm for mid-drives (Bosch Performance Line CX 85, Shimano EP8 85, Bosch Performance Line 75) versus 40–50 Nm for typical hub motors.

prov.quote: Torque is the number to look at

concepts.title: Go mid-drive
concepts.summary: For the 8 percent hill, a mid-drive is the safer bet: shifting down keeps cadence, meaning less effort and less sweat. A good hub motor would cope at moderate speed.

prov.quote: Then a mid-drive is the safer bet.

concepts.title: Bosch & Shimano systems
concepts.summary: Rated more refined by independent tests: smoother power, better sensors and software, and a larger dealer network for warranty repairs.

prov.quote: Independent tests generally rate Bosch and Shimano systems as more refined

concepts.title: Which e-bike should I buy?
concepts.summary: Answer: the Alder C5, the best all-rounder for hill climbing, weight, maintenance and theft protection, chosen over the Birch Metro 8 and Cedar Urban.

prov.quote: I'll go with the Alder.

concepts.title: Bafang
concepts.summary: Motor maker whose strengths are price and openness (cheaper parts, more shops can work on them); weaker on polished power delivery, with more variation between bike makers' setups.

prov.quote: Bafang's advantage is price and openness

concepts.title: Bosch batteries beat Bafang
concepts.summary: The reader's claim that Bosch batteries are better than Bafang's; only partly true, since most brands use the same few cell makers.

prov.quote: I read that Bosch batteries are better than Bafang.

concepts.title: Cells matter, not the brand
concepts.summary: Most brands use cells from Samsung, LG or Panasonic; battery life depends more on the cells and charging habits than on the brand on the case.

prov.quote: Battery life depends more on the cells and how you charge them than on the brand

concepts.title: Dealer network is the real point
concepts.summary: For a daily commuter where downtime matters, Bosch/Shimano's dealer network for warranty repairs matters more than any battery difference.

prov.quote: the dealer network is the real point, more than the battery

concepts.title: Battery size
concepts.summary: For 28 km a day with a hill, 400–500 Wh gives a couple of days between charges, even in winter.

prov.quote: 400 to 500 Wh gives a couple of days between charges in winter

concepts.title: Battery lifespan
concepts.summary: A 500 Wh battery keeps about 80% capacity after 500–800 full cycles; at one cycle every two days that's 3–4 years, so a 600–800 replacement may come near the end of three years.

prov.quote: keeps about 80 percent of its capacity after 500 to 800 full cycles

concepts.title: Belt drive
concepts.summary: A carbon-reinforced rubber belt replacing the chain: no oil, no rust, lasts 2–3× as long (about 15,000–20,000 km). Needs an internal gear hub. Worth it for a rain-riding daily commuter.

prov.quote: A belt drive replaces the chain with a carbon-reinforced rubber belt.

concepts.title: Internal gear hub
concepts.summary: Gears sealed inside the rear hub; required for a belt. Trade-offs: fewer gears, slightly more friction, needs a knowledgeable shop, and rear flats are fiddlier.

prov.quote: It only works with an internal gear hub

concepts.title: Chain and cassette
concepts.summary: Conventional drivetrain with more gears; chains wear out every 3,000–4,000 km and cassettes every other chain, and need cleaning and oiling.

prov.quote: chains every 3,000 to 4,000 km

concepts.title: Step-through or diamond frame?
concepts.summary: Still open. Step-through is easier with a bag and work clothes; a diamond frame is stiffer and lighter.

prov.quote: step-through is easier with a bag and in work clothes

concepts.title: First service & battery warranty
concepts.summary: Ask the shop about the first service (usually free after 500 km) and the battery warranty (usually 2 years).

prov.quote: usually free after 500 km

concepts.title: Dogwood Hub
concepts.summary: Hub-motor contrast option: 45 Nm rear hub, 418 Wh, 7-speed, 21 kg, about 1,700; not worth close comparison. Name may be illustrative.

prov.quote: The ones worth comparing closely are the first three.

concepts.title: No bike wins everything
concepts.summary: Alder is the best all-rounder for the reader's list; Birch if maintenance matters more than stairs; Cedar to save about 1,000.

prov.quote: No bike wins everything. The Alder is the best all-rounder for your list

concepts.title: Three-year running cost
concepts.summary: At 6,000 km/year: chain bikes about 850 (≈5 chains, 2–3 cassettes, 4 sets of pads, two services a year); belt bike quoted at about 650, though its listed items sum nearer 730. Excludes a possible battery replacement.

prov.quote: About 850 over three years.

concepts.title: Belt saves little
concepts.summary: Over three years the belt saves maybe 200 (likely closer to 100–150 when the figures are summed); not a big factor either way.

prov.quote: the belt saves maybe 200 over three years, not a huge amount

concepts.title: Removable battery
concepts.summary: All four bikes have one: take it inside at work to deter theft, and remove it (about 2.5–3 kg) before carrying the bike upstairs.

prov.quote: A removable battery (all four have one)

concepts.title: D-lock plus front-wheel cable
concepts.summary: Buy a Sold Secure Gold or Diamond rated D-lock plus a cable for the front wheel. Not yet bought.

prov.quote: a Sold Secure Gold or Diamond D-lock plus a cable for the front wheel

concepts.title: Cedar is the fallback
concepts.summary: If the Alder's test ride goes badly (stairs, sizing), the lighter, cheaper Cedar Urban is the natural alternative.

prov.quote: the Cedar if you'd rather save 1,000

concepts.title: Hub motor
concepts.summary: Motor in the rear (or front) wheel: cheaper, quieter, lower maintenance, but struggles on long steep climbs. Typically 40–50 Nm.

prov.quote: it's cheaper, quieter, and needs less maintenance, but struggles on long steep climbs

concepts.title: Mid-drive motor
concepts.summary: Motor at the pedals that drives the chain and uses the bike's gears; climbs far better and feels natural. Typically 60–85 Nm.

prov.quote: a mid-drive motor sits at the pedals and drives the chain

concepts.title: Motor drives through the gears
concepts.summary: A mid-drive turns the chain, so you can shift down on a climb and keep your cadence: less effort, less sweat.

prov.quote: drives the chain, so it uses the bike's gears
lets you shift down and keep cadence, which means less effort and less sweat

concepts.title: Motor noise
concepts.summary: How much sound the motor makes on the ride; hub motors are the quieter kind.

prov.quote: it's cheaper, quieter, and needs less maintenance

concepts.title: Motor maintenance needs
concepts.summary: How much upkeep the motor system asks for; hub motors need less than mid-drives.

prov.quote: needs less maintenance
I care most about: hill climbing, low maintenance

concepts.summary: Shimano EP6 85 Nm, 504 Wh, Nexus 5 internal hub with belt drive, 26 kg, about 3,400. Lowest maintenance but heaviest mid-drive. Name may be illustrative.

concepts.title: Alder C5
concepts.summary: The chosen bike: Bosch Performance Line 75 Nm, 500 Wh, 10-speed chain, mudguards and rack, 24 kg, about 3,200; supports Bosch's app motor lock. Name may be illustrative.

prov.quote: I'll go with the Alder.
